    "**Rating**: Buy\n\n"
    "**Executive Summary**: Enter a full position now.\n\n"
    "**Investment Thesis**: The setup looks strong. I am committing to Buy."
)

# Analyst reports are non-empty so the baseline graph produces a full run; they
# are deliberately generic prose and cite no evidence IDs (the baseline has no
# such concept anyway).
ANALYST_REPORT = "Analysis prose for this run. No structured evidence references are present."
RESEARCH_PLAN = "**Recommendation**: Buy\n\n**Rationale**: Bullish.\n\n**Strategic Actions**: Add."
TRADER_PLAN = "FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **BUY**"
DEBATER_ARGUMENT = "Analyst: the case is made from the reports above."


class _BuyNoEvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):
    """A fake chat model that always answers BUY_NO_EVIDENCE_DECISION.

    It reports no tool calls (so an analyst's turn ends with its report) and it
    declines structured output (so the Portfolio Manager takes the baseline's
    free-text path — the exact path FR-01 says must not bypass the gate). Using
    the real free-text path keeps this counterexample honest: the leak it exposes
    is the baseline's, not one manufactured by the test.
    """

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "buy-no-evidence-fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        # Analysts must not loop on tool calls: stay the same model, but every
        # reply reports no tool_calls, so take_turn ends the analyst's turn.
        return self

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        # Force the free-text fallback in bind_structured()/invoke_structured().
        raise NotImplementedError("structured output disabled for counterexample")

    def _generate(
        self,
        messages,
        stop=None,
        run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> ChatResult:
        message = AIMessage(content=BUY_NO_EVIDENCE_DECISION)
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=message)])


class _FakeClient:
    """Stand-in for a provider client: ``get_llm()`` returns the fake model."""

    def __init__(self, llm):
        self._llm = llm

    def get_llm(self):
        return self._llm


def _run_through_propagate(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Drive the real propagate() path offline and return (signal, memory_log).

    ``create_tier_client`` is patched in the trading_graph module namespace so
    the graph builds with the fake model instead of touching any provider. All
    on-disk state (cache, results, memory) goes to ``tmp_path``.
    """
    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg

    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "create_tier_client", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_BuyNoEvidenceModel()))

    config = {
        "data_cache_dir": str(tmp_path / "cache"),
        "results_dir": str(tmp_path / "results"),
        "memory_log_path": str(tmp_path / "memory.md"),
        "checkpoint_enabled": False,
    }

    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(
        selected_analysts=("market",),
        debug=False,

    """Exit 1 — Python API: a legal Buy with no valid evidence must not be returned.

def test_buy_without_evidence_is_not_written_to_decision_memory(monkeypatch, tmp_path):

"""Deterministic publication gate for FR-01 / INV-01.

Owner module for the release decision described in
``architecture-blueprint.md`` (FR-01 row) and ``docs/architecture/invariants.md``
(INV-01). The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation
becomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the
program itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating
fallback is honoured around the gate.

Design (plan revision 1):
- Evidence is indexed from the run's own non-empty analyst reports *before* the
  first debate turn, so every accepted argument cites material that exists in
  this run.
- Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against
  the run index and only then mints an ``argument_id`` for the accepted argument.
- The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.
- ``evaluate`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted argument ->
  this run's material) and returns one ``GateOutcome``. ``apply`` projects that
  outcome onto the run state used by the sinks (CLI, API, reports, memory).

Only two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and
``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references
all map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,
``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER, RATING_REVIEW

# The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.
_ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (
    "market_report",
    "sentiment_report",
    "news_report",
    "fundamentals_report",
)

# Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).
INVALID_RATING = "INVALID_RATING"
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE"

# The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.
_RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)

# Publication status values carried on the run state.
APPROVED = "APPROVED"
BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EvidenceRecord:
    """One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id."""

    evidence_id: str
    source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. "market_report"
    excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material
    run_id: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ArgumentRecord:
    """An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run."""

    argument_id: str
    speaker: str                  # "Bull Analyst" / "Bear Analyst"
    text: str
    evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GateOutcome:
    """The single release decision for a run."""

    status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED
    reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
    rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED
    resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
    # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)

    @property
    def approved(self) -> bool:
        return self.status == APPROVED


class EvidenceIndex:
    """Run-scoped evidence and accepted arguments built by the program.

    Constructed at the start of a run from its own analyst reports, so ids from a
    different run can never resolve here. Immutable after build; ``accept`` adds
    accepted arguments but never rewrites evidence.
    """

    def __init__(self, run_id: str, evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord]):
        self.run_id = run_id
        self._evidence = dict(evidence)
        self._arguments: dict[str, ArgumentRecord] = {}

    # --- evidence ---

    def has_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:
        return evidence_id in self._evidence

    def evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> EvidenceRecord:
        return self._evidence[evidence_id]

    @property
    def evidence_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(self._evidence)

    # --- accepted arguments ---

    def accept(self, argument: ArgumentRecord) -> bool:
        """Accept an argument iff every cited evidence id resolves in this run.

        Returns whether it was accepted. Rejection leaves the index unchanged;
        the caller must not mint an argument id for a rejected submission.
        """
        if not argument.evidence_ids:
            return False
        if any(eid not in self._evidence for eid in argument.evidence_ids):
            return False
        self._arguments[argument.argument_id] = argument
        return True

    def has_argument(self, argument_id: str) -> bool:
        return argument_id in self._arguments

    def argument(self, argument_id: str) -> ArgumentRecord:
        return self._arguments[argument_id]

    @property
    def argument_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(self._arguments)


def build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:
    """Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.

    Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and
    iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.
    """
    evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}
    for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:
        text = state.get(key)
        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
            continue
        evidence_id = f"ev:{run_id}:{key}"
        excerpt = _excerpt(text)
        evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(
            evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=excerpt, run_id=run_id,
        )
    return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)


def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:
    """A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only)."""
    flat = " ".join(text.split())
    return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + "\u2026"


def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:
    """The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.

    Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.
    ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.
    """
    if value is None:
        return None
    rating = getattr(value, "value", value)
    if not isinstance(rating, str):
        return None
    return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None


def evaluate(
    index: EvidenceIndex,
    candidate_rating,
    candidate_argument_ids,
) -> GateOutcome:
    """Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.

    Order matters: an invalid rating is reported before a missing chain, so a
    candidate that fails both returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is
    consulted here.
    """
    rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)
    if rating is None:
        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)

    cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)
    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for argument_id in cited:
        if not index.has_argument(argument_id):
            continue
        argument = index.argument(argument_id)
        for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:
            if index.has_evidence(evidence_id):
                resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, index.evidence(evidence_id).source))
    if not resolved:
        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)

    return GateOutcome(
        status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),
    )


def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:
    """Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.

    On APPROVED the official rating and the resolved chain are published. On
    BLOCKED the run carries no official rating (``final_rating`` becomes the
    non-tradeable sentinel) and no candidate body reaches an official field; the
    candidate decision is kept only in the internal ``candidate_decision`` key for
    audit and is never read by a sink.
    """
    status = outcome.status
    final_state["publication_status"] = status
    final_state["publication_reason"] = outcome.reason
    final_state["publication_chain"] = outcome.resolved_chain

    # The candidate body is moved out of the official decision field, so a sink
    # cannot publish it as the run's recommendation.
    candidate_body = final_state.pop("final_trade_decision", None) or final_state.get(
        "candidate_decision"
    )
    if candidate_body:
        final_state["candidate_decision"] = candidate_body
    final_state.pop("final_trade_decision", None)

    if outcome.approved:
        final_state["final_rating"] = outcome.rating
        final_state["final_trade_decision"] = candidate_body or ""
    else:
        # No tradeable rating leaks: the sentinel keeps legacy readers safe when
        # they guard with ``is_review``.
        final_state["final_rating"] = RATING_REVIEW
        final_state["final_trade_decision"] = ""
    return final_state

"""FR-01 publication gate — unit tests on the deterministic chain checks.

These exercise ``tradingagents.graph.publication_gate`` directly with fixed,
in-memory material (no model, no network). They cover the normal case and each
negative case from the D1 acceptance criteria: invalid rating, missing reference,
unknown id, cross-run reference, and missing/unparseable evidence.

Expected after implementation: all pass. Before implementation the module did not
exist, so these tests could not run (import error) — they are behaviour tests, not
the baseline counterexample.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate

RATINGS = gate.RATINGS_5_TIER


def _state(run_reports=None):
    """A minimal run state with the given analyst reports."""
    return dict(run_reports or {})


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_valid_rating_with_resolvable_evidence_is_approved():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({
        "market_report": "Price broke out above the 50-day average.",
    }))
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    assert index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(
        argument_id="arg:bull:1", speaker="Bull Analyst", text="breakout",
        evidence_ids=(ev,),
    ))

    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ("arg:bull:1",))

    assert outcome.status == gate.APPROVED
    assert outcome.rating == "Buy"
    assert outcome.resolved_chain == (("arg:bull:1", ev, "market_report"),)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_invalid_rating_is_blocked_with_invalid_rating():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Strong Buy", ())
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INVALID_RATING


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_missing_reference_is_blocked_with_insufficient_evidence():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ())
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_unknown_argument_id_is_blocked():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ("arg:does-not-exist",))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_unknown_evidence_id_is_not_accepted():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    assert index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(
        argument_id="arg:bull:1", speaker="Bull Analyst", text="x",
        evidence_ids=("ev:other-run:market_report",),
    )) is False
    assert index.argument_ids == ()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cross_run_reference_is_blocked():
    run_a = gate.build_evidence_index("run-A", _state({"market_report": "a"}))
    ev_a = run_a.evidence_ids[0]
    # An argument minted in run A cannot be accepted in run B.
    run_b = gate.build_evidence_index("run-B", _state({"market_report": "b"}))
    assert run_b.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(
        argument_id="arg:bull:1", speaker="Bull Analyst", text="x", evidence_ids=(ev_a,),
    )) is False
    outcome = gate.evaluate(run_b, "Buy", ("arg:bull:1",))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_missing_evidence_material_yields_no_index():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "   ", "news_report": ""}))
    assert index.evidence_ids == ()
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ("arg:bull:1",))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_invalid_rating_takes_precedence_over_missing_evidence():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, None, ())
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INVALID_RATING


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_apply_blocks_candidate_and_hides_body():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    final_state = {"final_trade_decision": "**Rating**: Buy\n\nbuy now", "final_rating": "Buy"}
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ())
    gate.apply(outcome, final_state)

    assert final_state["publication_status"] == gate.BLOCKED
    assert final_state["publication_reason"] == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
    assert final_state["final_rating"] == gate.RATING_REVIEW
    assert final_state["final_trade_decision"] == ""
    assert final_state["candidate_decision"] == "**Rating**: Buy\n\nbuy now"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_apply_publishes_approved_rating_and_chain():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", _state({"market_report": "text"}))
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord("arg:bull:1", "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev,)))
    final_state = {"final_trade_decision": "**Rating**: Buy\n\nbuy now"}
    outcome = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ("arg:bull:1",))
    gate.apply(outcome, final_state)

    assert final_state["publication_status"] == gate.APPROVED
    assert final_state["final_rating"] == "Buy"
    assert final_state["final_trade_decision"]
    assert final_state["publication_chain"] == (("arg:bull:1", ev, "market_report"),)

    into a concrete transaction proposal: should the desk execute a Buy, a
    Sell, or sit on Hold this round.  Position sizing and the nuanced
    Overweight / Underweight calls happen later at the Portfolio Manager.
    """

    BUY = "Buy"
    HOLD = "Hold"
    SELL = "Sell"

    """A Bull or Bear argument with structured evidence references.

    FR-01: the researcher may only cite evidence IDs that exist in this run's
    program-built index. The program validates these IDs and mints an argument
    ID only for an accepted argument; unverified prose is not a release path.

        description=(

            "resolvable ID cannot support a published recommendation."

So `invoke_structured(None,...)` returns None → plain `llm.invoke(prompt).content` → the buy-no-evidence text. PM `bind_structured` also None → plain path → `argument_ids=[]` → gate blocks. 

But the counterexample asserts on `propagate()` which now calls `publish`. Good. However the counterexample fake model's `_generate` always returns BUY text for **every** node including analysts/researchers; researchers now call `llm.invoke` → BUY text as argument, evidence_ids empty → no acceptance. PM → BUY, no args → BLOCKED. 

Now `publication_gate.apply` pops `final_trade_decision` then re-sets it empty on block — but `_log_state` runs in `record_decision` **after** publish, so state log sees `""`. Good. Also `run_rating` returns `final_rating=REVIEW` → API returns REVIEW. Counterexample `signal != "Buy"` passes now.

Let me verify `apply` ordering bug: it does `candidate_body = final_state.pop("final_trade_decision", ...)` then later `final_state["final_trade_decision"] = ""`. Good. But on APPROVED it sets `final_trade_decision = candidate_body or ""`. Good.

One issue: `evaluate` reads `final_state.get("candidate_argument_ids")`. In the unit test `test_apply_*` I call `evaluate(index, "Buy", ())` directly — fine.

"""INV-01 four-exit test — a blocked Buy leaks nowhere.

FR-01 / INV-01: a candidate rejected by the publication gate must not appear as
an official rating at any sink — Python API return, CLI display, Markdown report,
HTML report — nor be written to decision memory. This test drives the real
``TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()`` entry point (and the report writers) with the
fake no-evidence model, then checks each exit independently.

Expected after implementation: pass. Before implementation there was no gate, so
this is a behaviour test, not the baseline counterexample.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult

from tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree
from tradingagents.report_html import render_report

BUY_NO_EVIDENCE = "**Rating**: Buy\n\n**Executive Summary**: buy.\n\n**Investment Thesis**: buy."


class _BuyNoEvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):
    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "buy-no-evidence-fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        return self

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        raise NotImplementedError("structured output disabled")

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,
                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,
                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=BUY_NO_EVIDENCE))])


class _FakeClient:
    def __init__(self, llm):
        self._llm = llm

    def get_llm(self):
        return self._llm


def _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg
    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "create_tier_client", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_BuyNoEvidenceModel()))
    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "resolve_instrument_identity", lambda t: {
        "company_name": "NVIDIA Corporation", "sector": "Technology",
        "industry": "Semiconductors", "exchange": "NASDAQ", "quote_type": "EQUITY",
    })
    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    config.update({
        "data_cache_dir": str(tmp_path / "cache"),
        "results_dir": str(tmp_path / "results"),
        "memory_log_path": str(tmp_path / "memory.md"),
        "checkpoint_enabled": False,
    })
    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=("market",), debug=False, config=config)
    final_state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-05")
    return graph, final_state, signal


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_python_api_return_is_not_buy(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    _, _, signal = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    assert signal != "Buy"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_memory_has_no_entry(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    graph, _, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    assert graph.memory_log.load_entries() == []


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_final_state_carries_blocked_status(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    _, final_state, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    assert final_state.get("publication_status") == "BLOCKED"
    assert final_state.get("publication_reason") == "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE"
    assert final_state.get("final_trade_decision") == ""


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_markdown_report_shows_blocked_not_buy(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    _, final_state, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    path = write_report_tree(final_state, "NVDA", tmp_path / "report", settings=None, html=False)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "BLOCKED" in text
    assert "Rating: Buy" not in text


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_html_report_shows_blocked_not_buy(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    _, final_state, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    html = render_report("NVDA", final_state, None, [])
    assert "BLOCKED" in html
    assert ">Buy<" not in html

class _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):
    """Emits reports; structured calls return argument ids the test can pre-know.

    The Bull's structured evidence id must match the index build formula
    ``ev:<run_id>:market_report``. Since the run token is random, the model cites
    by a marker the test rewrites via ``self.cited`` — but the program validates
    against the real index, so we let the Bull cite the market evidence by its
    source and resolve it through the index the graph built.

    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "evidence-fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        return self

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        if schema is DebateArgument:
            return _StructuredArgument(self.cited)
        if schema is PortfolioDecision:
            return _StructuredDecision()
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,
                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,
                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])


class _StructuredArgument:
    def __init__(self, cited):
        self._cited = cited

    def invoke(self, prompt):
        return DebateArgument(argument="bull case", evidence_ids=list(self._cited))

    def invoke(self, prompt):
        # The PM must cite the argument the program accepted. The run token is
        # unknown here, so we cite by the deterministic argument id the Bull
        # mints (arg:bull:1) — the gate resolves it against accepted_arguments.
        return PortfolioDecision(

            executive_summary="add",
            investment_thesis="breakout",
            argument_ids=["arg:bull:1"],

Better: derive a stable run token from company+date so that resumed runs get the same token. But cross-run reference must still fail. def _run_token(state) -> str:
    """A deterministic token that binds this run's evidence and argument ids.

    Derived from the instrument and trade date, so a checkpointed run resumed on
    the same ticker+date rebuilds the identical ids (requirement 3). Ids stay
    run-bound because the index they belong to is rebuilt from that run's own
    reports; an argument minted in a different run is not in this run's index and
    is rejected as a cross-run reference.
    """
    return f"{state.get('company_of_interest', '?')}:{state.get('trade_date', '?')}"


def _index_evidence_node(state) -> dict:
    """FR-01: build this run's evidence index before the debate starts.

    The index is stored as plain, msgpack-safe data (``index_to_state``) so the
    checkpoint can serialize it; ``accepted_arguments`` starts empty and is filled
    as researchers submit validated evidence ids.
    """
    from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import build_evidence_index, index_to_state

    index = build_evidence_index(_run_token(state), state)
    return {"evidence_index": index_to_state(index), "accepted_arguments": []}

## Requirements
- Stay within the 12 approved business file paths (listed below); no permission changes, no commit/push.

- Fix all five items: (1) evidence menu in Bull/Bear prompts + run-bound `argument_id`; (2) publication boundary: PM writes internal candidate only, BLOCKED Python return has no `candidate_decision`/official rating, REVIEW only in tuple member 2, status JSON records BLOCKED+reason, memory writes nothing; (3) checkpoint serialization: graph state must be msgpack-safe (no `EvidenceIndex` object), verify resumed runs still validate the chain; (4) CLI test must capture real Rich render and drive streaming entry, verifying pre-verdict hiding, post-approval showing, BLOCKED+reason on refusal, and list affected old tests needing human approval before changing frozen tests; (5) fix Ruff import ordering.

"""INV-01 CLI test — the candidate is not shown before the gate, only after approval.

FR-01 / INV-01: the CLI must not surface the Portfolio Manager candidate as an
official recommendation while the stream is still running; only after the gate
approves may the official decision be shown, and a refused candidate shows BLOCKED
with its reason and nothing else.

This test captures the **actual Rich render** (a ``Console(record=True)`` swapped
into ``cli.display.console``, exported as text) rather than monkeypatching
``console.print``. It also drives the **streaming entry point's update decisions**:
the exact ``investment_debate_state`` / ``risk_debate_state`` chunk handling from
``cli/run.py`` is replayed through the real ``MessageBuffer`` that the CLI uses.

No network, no model, no Live screen.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from rich.console import Console

from cli import display
from cli.display import MessageBuffer, display_complete_report

CANDIDATE_BODY = "**Rating**: Buy\n\n**Executive Summary**: buy now.\n\n**Investment Thesis**: buy."


def _record_render(monkeypatch):
    """Swap a recording console into cli.display and return a text exporter."""
    record_console = Console(record=True, width=120, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)

    def render_text():
        return record_console.export_text()

    monkeypatch.setattr(display, "console", record_console)
    return render_text


def _apply_stream_chunk(buffer: MessageBuffer, chunk: dict) -> None:
    """Replay the streaming entry's decision-surfacing logic for one chunk.

    Mirrors the ``cl chunk.get("risk_debate_state")`` branch in ``cli/run.py``:
    the research/risk debate sections update, but the Portfolio Manager's
    candidate is never written into the decision panel before the gate.
    """
    if chunk.get("investment_debate_state"):
        debate = chunk["investment_debate_state"]
        if debate.get("bull_history"):
            buffer.update_report_section(
                "investment_plan", f"### Bull Researcher Analysis\n{debate['bull_history']}"
            )
        if debate.get("bear_history"):
            buffer.update_report_section(
                "investment_plan", f"### Bear Researcher Analysis\n{debate['bear_history']}"
            )
        if chunk.get("investment_plan"):
            buffer.update_report_section(
                "investment_plan", f"### Research Manager Decision\n{chunk['investment_plan']}"
            )

    if chunk.get("risk_debate_state"):
        risk = chunk["risk_debate_state"]
        for hist_key, title in (
            ("aggressive_history", "Aggressive Analyst"),
            ("conservative_history", "Conservative Analyst"),
            ("neutral_history", "Neutral Analyst"),
        ):
            if risk.get(hist_key):
                buffer.update_report_section(
                    "final_trade_decision",
                    f"### {title} Analysis\n{risk[hist_key]}",
                )
        # The candidate (chunk["final_trade_decision"]) is deliberately NOT written
        # here — that is what FR-01 requires before the gate runs.


def _new_buffer():
    buffer = MessageBuffer()
    buffer.init_for_analysis(["market"])
    return buffer


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_streaming_never_surfaces_candidate_before_verdict(monkeypatch):
    """Before the gate, the decision panel shows debate only, never the candidate."""
    buffer = _new_buffer()
    # A stream chunk carrying the PM candidate and the risk debate.
    chunk = {
        "risk_debate_state": {
            "aggressive_history": "aggressive case",
            "conservative_history": "conservative case",
            "neutral_history": "neutral case",
        },
        "final_trade_decision": CANDIDATE_BODY,
    }
    _apply_stream_chunk(buffer, chunk)

    panel = buffer.report_sections.get("final_trade_decision") or ""
    assert "aggressive case" in panel or "neutral case" in panel
    # The candidate body must not be in the decision panel pre-verdict.
    assert CANDIDATE_BODY not in panel
    assert "buy now" not in panel


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_blocked_state_shows_only_blocked_and_reason(monkeypatch):
    """After a refusal, the rendered report shows BLOCKED + reason, never the body."""
    render_text = _record_render(monkeypatch)

    final_state = {
        "publication_status": "BLOCKED",
        "publication_reason": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
        "final_trade_decision": "",            # apply() emptied the official field
        "candidate_decision": CANDIDATE_BODY,  # internal only, must not render
    }
    display_complete_report(final_state)

    text = render_text()
    assert "BLOCKED" in text
    assert "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE" in text
    assert "buy now" not in text
    assert "Rating" not in text or "Buy" not in text.split("BLOCKED")[-1]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_approved_state_shows_official_decision(monkeypatch):
    """After approval, the rendered report shows the official decision body."""
    render_text = _record_render(monkeypatch)

    final_state = {
        "publication_status": "APPROVED",
        "publication_reason": None,
        "final_trade_decision": CANDIDATE_BODY,
    }
    display_complete_report(final_state)

    assert "buy now" in render_text()

"""FR-01 positive test — a valid rating with resolvable evidence is released.

The normal case: a decision that cites an accepted argument whose evidence id
exists in this run's index publishes as an official rating, and the chain resolves
back to the run material. This guards against a gate that blocks everything.

The fake model does **not** receive a pre-injected evidence id: it reads the
``Available evidence`` block out of the prompt it is actually given and cites the
first id it finds — so the test proves the prompt wiring, not an injected constant.

It also proves the argument id is run-bound: an argument id minted under a
different run token is rejected (see ``test_cross_run_argument_is_rejected``).

Drives the real ``TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()`` path.
No network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import pytest
from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult

from tradingagents.agents.schemas import DebateArgument, PortfolioDecision, PortfolioRating

REPORT = "The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend."

# A line in the evidence menu looks like: "- ev:<run>:market_report  [market_report] <excerpt>"
_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^- (ev:\S+)\s+\[", re.MULTILINE)


def _cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[str]:
    """The evidence IDs the researcher is actually offered in this prompt."""
    match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)
    return [match.group(1)] if match else []


class _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):
    """Emits reports; structured calls read the evidence menu from the prompt."""

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "evidence-fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        return self

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        if schema is DebateArgument:
            return _StructuredArgument()
        if schema is PortfolioDecision:
            return _StructuredDecision()
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,
                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,
                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])


class _StructuredArgument:
    def invoke(self, prompt):
        # Cite the real run evidence id that appears in the prompt.
        return DebateArgument(
            argument="bull case",
            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt),
        )


class _StructuredDecision:
    def invoke(self, prompt):
        # The PM must cite the accepted argument. The argument id is run-bound, so
        # read it from the 'Accepted arguments' block the PM is actually given.
        match = re.search(r"^- (arg:\S+)", prompt, re.MULTILINE)
        argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []
        return PortfolioDecision(
            rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,
            executive_summary="add",
            investment_thesis="breakout",
            argument_ids=argument_ids,
        )


class _FakeClient:
    def __init__(self, llm):
        self._llm = llm

    def get_llm(self):
        return self._llm


def _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg
    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "create_tier_client", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_EvidenceModel()))
    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "resolve_instrument_identity", lambda t: {
        "company_name": "NVIDIA Corporation", "sector": "Technology",
        "industry": "Semiconductors", "exchange": "NASDAQ", "quote_type": "EQUITY",
    })
    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    config.update({
        "data_cache_dir": str(tmp_path / "cache"),
        "results_dir": str(tmp_path / "results"),
        "memory_log_path": str(tmp_path / "memory.md"),
        "checkpoint_enabled": False,
    })
    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=("market",), debug=False, config=config)
    final_state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-05")
    return graph, final_state, signal


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_valid_rating_with_resolvable_evidence_is_approved(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    graph, final_state, signal = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)

    assert final_state.get("publication_status") == "APPROVED", final_state.get("publication_reason")
    assert signal == "Buy"
    assert final_state.get("publication_chain")  # resolves back to run material
    assert graph.memory_log.load_entries()  # an approved decision is recorded


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_argument_id_is_run_bound(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """The accepted argument id embeds the run id, so it cannot be reused cross-run."""
    _, final_state, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    chain = final_state.get("publication_chain") or []
    assert chain, "expected a resolved chain"
    argument_id = chain[0][0]
    assert argument_id.startswith("arg:bull:")
    assert "NVDA:2026-01-05" in argument_id

1: """Shared helpers for invoking an agent with structured output and a graceful fallback.
2: 
3: The Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same
4: canonical pattern:
5: 
6: 1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``
7:    so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does
8:    not support structured output (rare; mostly older Ollama models), the
9:    wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.
10: 2. At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to
11:    markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason
12:    (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall
13:    back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.
14: 
15: Centralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures
16: all three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import logging
22: from collections.abc import Callable
23: from typing import Any, TypeVar
24: 
25: from pydantic import BaseModel
26: 
27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
28: 
29: T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)
30: 
31: # Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a
32: # model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole
33: # structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path
34: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone
35: # (#1130).
36: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (
37:     "Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools "
38:     "or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly."
39: )
40: 
41: 
42: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:
43:     """Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.
44: 
45:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent
46:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.
47:     """
48:     try:
49:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)
50:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:
51:         logger.warning(
52:             "%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); "
53:             "falling back to free-text generation",
54:             agent_name, exc,
55:         )
56:         return None
57: 
58: 
59: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:
60:     """Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.
61: 
62:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat
63:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that
64:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.
65:     """
66:     if structured_llm is None:
67:         return None
68:     try:
69:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)
70:         if result is None:
71:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling
72:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it
73:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.
74:             raise ValueError("structured output returned no parsed result")
75:         return result
76:     except Exception as exc:
77:         logger.warning(
78:             "%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text",
79:             agent_name, exc,
80:         )
81:         return None
82: 
83: 
84: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(
85:     structured_llm: Any | None,
86:     plain_llm: Any,
87:     prompt: Any,
88:     render: Callable[[T], str],
89:     agent_name: str,
90: ) -> str:
91:     """Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure."""
92:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)
93:     if result is not None:
94:         return render(result)
95:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content

"""INV-01 checkpoint test — the evidence chain survives a serialization round-trip.

FR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a checkpointed run must be resumable, so the graph
state's ``evidence_index`` must be plain, msgpack-safe data — not an ``EvidenceIndex``
object (the baseline error was ``TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable:
EvidenceIndex``). After a round-trip through msgpack, ``evaluate`` must still resolve
the same chain and reach the same release decision.

Also proves the run-bound argument id is stable across the round-trip (so a resumed
run can still cite the argument the pre-interruption debate accepted).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import msgpack
import pytest

from tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate


def _roundtrip(value):
    """Serialize and deserialize a value the way a checkpoint does (msgpack)."""
    return msgpack.unpackb(msgpack.packb(value), raw=False)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_state_index_is_msgpack_safe():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", {"market_report": "breakout text"})
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord("arg:bull:run-1:1", "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev,)))

    state_index = gate.index_to_state(index)
    # The whole point of requirement 3: this must not raise.
    restored = _roundtrip(state_index)

    assert restored["run_id"] == "run-1"
    assert restored["evidence"][0]["id"] == ev
    assert restored["arguments"][0]["evidence_ids"] == [ev]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_chain_still_validates_after_roundtrip():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", {"market_report": "breakout text"})
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord("arg:bull:run-1:1", "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev,)))

    restored = _roundtrip(gate.index_to_state(index))

    outcome = gate.evaluate(restored, "Buy", ("arg:bull:run-1:1",))
    assert outcome.status == gate.APPROVED
    assert outcome.resolved_chain == (("arg:bull:run-1:1", ev, "market_report"),)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_roundtrip_keeps_the_block_on_a_missing_chain():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", {"market_report": "breakout text"})
    restored = _roundtrip(gate.index_to_state(index))

    outcome = gate.evaluate(restored, "Buy", ("arg:bull:run-1:1",))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_state_dict_and_object_read_the_same():
    index = gate.build_evidence_index("run-1", {"market_report": "breakout text"})
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord("arg:bull:run-1:1", "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev,)))

    from_object = gate.evaluate(index, "Buy", ("arg:bull:run-1:1",))
    from_dict = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(index), "Buy", ("arg:bull:run-1:1",))
    assert from_object == from_dict

            _Graph.publish_calls += 1
            from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import apply, evaluate

            outcome = evaluate(final_state.get("evidence_index"), final_state.get("candidate_rating"), ())

            yield [], {

def _new_run_id() -> str:
    """A fresh identifier minted once per run, unique across runs.

    Not derived from ticker+date: two independent runs on the same instrument and
    day must have different ids so one cannot cite the other's evidence. It is
    generated with ``uuid4`` and stored in the serializable graph state, then
    reused verbatim on resume (see ``_index_evidence_node``), so a resumed run keeps
    the same id.
    """
    import uuid

    return uuid.uuid4().hex


def _index_evidence_node(state) -> dict:
    """FR-01: build this run's evidence index before the debate starts.

    The run id is minted here once and stored on the state; a resumed run reuses
    the id already present instead of minting a new one, so ids stay stable across
    an interruption. The index is stored as plain, msgpack-safe data
    (``index_to_state``) so the checkpoint can serialize it; ``accepted_arguments``
    starts empty and is filled as researchers submit validated evidence ids.
    """
    from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import build_evidence_index, index_to_state

    run_id = state.get("run_id") or _new_run_id()
    index = build_evidence_index(run_id, state)
    return {"run_id": run_id, "evidence_index": index_to_state(index), "accepted_arguments": []}

def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:
    """Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.

    On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the
    candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the
    returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,
    candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so
    the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The
    only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the
    caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.
    """
    status = outcome.status
    final_state["publication_status"] = status
    final_state["publication_reason"] = outcome.reason
    final_state["publication_chain"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)

    if outcome.approved:
        body = final_state.get("candidate_decision") or final_state.get("final_trade_decision") or ""
        final_state["final_rating"] = outcome.rating
        final_state["final_trade_decision"] = body
        final_state.pop("candidate_decision", None)
        final_state.pop("candidate_rating", None)
        final_state.pop("candidate_argument_ids", None)
    else:
        # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating
        # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather
        # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.
        final_state["final_rating"] = ""
        final_state["final_trade_decision"] = ""
        final_state.pop("candidate_decision", None)
        final_state.pop("candidate_rating", None)
        final_state.pop("candidate_argument_ids", None)
    return final_state

"""INV-01 CLI test — the candidate is not shown before the gate, only after approval.

FR-01 / INV-01: the CLI must not surface the Portfolio Manager candidate as an
official recommendation while the stream is still running; only after the gate
approves may the official decision be shown, and a refused candidate shows BLOCKED
with its reason and nothing else.

These tests drive the **real** streaming entry ``cli.run.run_analysis`` with a fake
graph whose ``stream_run`` yields chunks carrying the candidate. They keep the real
``update_display`` so the live view is built for real, and snapshot the actual Rich
``Layout`` after every refresh — so assertions read the live view and message area,
not an empty stand-in console.

No network, no model, no real terminal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from rich.console import Console

import cli.display as display
import cli.run as cli_run
from cli.display import MessageBuffer, display_complete_report
from cli.models import AnalystType

CANDIDATE_BODY = (
    "**Rating**: Buy\n\n**Executive Summary**: buy now.\n\n**Investment Thesis**: buy."
)


def _render_layout(layout) -> str:
    """Render a Rich ``Layout`` to plain text the way the terminal would show it."""
    console = Console(record=True, width=200, height=60, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)
    console.print(layout)
    return console.export_text()


def _fake_graph(monkeypatch, chunks):
    """A graph whose stream yields ``chunks``; ``publish`` runs the real gate."""

    class _Graph:
        publish_calls = 0
        publish_status = None

        def create_run_state(self, *a, **k):
            return {"messages": []}

        def record_decision(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def get_graph_args(self, callbacks=None):
            return {}

        def begin_checkpoint(self, *a, **k):
            return None

        def checkpoint_input(self, state):
            return state

        def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def end_checkpoint(self):
            pass

        def publish(self, final_state):
            from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import apply, evaluate

            _Graph.publish_calls += 1
            outcome = evaluate(
                final_state.get("evidence_index"),
                final_state.get("candidate_rating"),
                final_state.get("candidate_argument_ids") or (),
            )
            apply(outcome, final_state)
            _Graph.publish_status = outcome.status
            return outcome.status

        def stream_run(self, *a, **k):
            for chunk in chunks:
                yield [], chunk

    fake = _Graph()
    fake.graph = fake
    fake.propagator = fake
    return fake


def _wire(monkeypatch, fake, snapshots):
    """Install the fake graph and capture the real live view after each refresh."""

    real_update = display.update_display

    def spy_update(layout, *a, **k):
        real_update(layout, *a, **k)
        snapshots.append(_render_layout(layout))

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "TradingAgentsGraph", lambda *a, **k: fake)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "update_display", spy_update)

def test_blocked_candidate_is_never_shown_and_only_blocked_renders(tmp_path_, monkeypatch):
    """A refused candidate never appears in the live view; BLOCKED + reason does."""
    snapshots = []
    final_render = {"text": ""}

"""INV-01 CLI test — the candidate is not shown before the gate, only after approval.

FR-01 / INV-01: the CLI must not surface the Portfolio Manager candidate as an
official recommendation while the stream is still running; only after the gate
approves may the official decision be shown, and a refused candidate shows BLOCKED
with its reason and nothing else.

These tests drive the **real** streaming entry ``cli.run.run_analysis`` with a fake
graph whose ``stream_run`` yields chunks carrying the candidate. They keep the real
``update_display`` so the live view is built for real, and snapshot the actual Rich
``Layout`` after every refresh — so assertions read the live view and message area,
not an empty stand-in console.

No network, no model, no real terminal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from rich.console import Console

import cli.display as display
import cli.run as cli_run
from cli.display import display_complete_report
from cli.models import AnalystType

CANDIDATE_BODY = (
    "**Rating**: Buy\n\n**Executive Summary**: buy now.\n\n**Investment Thesis**: buy."
)


def _render_layout(layout) -> str:
    """Render a Rich ``Layout`` to plain text the way the terminal would show it."""
    console = Console(record=True, width=200, height=60, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)
    console.print(layout)
    return console.export_text()


def _fake_graph(chunks):
    """A graph whose stream yields ``chunks``; ``publish`` runs the real gate."""

    class _Graph:
        publish_calls = 0
        publish_status = None

        def create_run_state(self, *a, **k):
            return {"messages": []}

        def record_decision(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def get_graph_args(self, callbacks=None):
            return {}

        def begin_checkpoint(self, *a, **k):
            return None

        def checkpoint_input(self, state):
            return state

        def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def end_checkpoint(self):
            pass

        def publish(self, final_state):
            from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import apply, evaluate

            _Graph.publish_calls += 1
            outcome = evaluate(
                final_state.get("evidence_index"),
                final_state.get("candidate_rating"),
                final_state.get("candidate_argument_ids") or (),
            )
            apply(outcome, final_state)
            _Graph.publish_status = outcome.status
            return outcome.status

        def stream_run(self, *a, **k):
            for chunk in chunks:
                yield [], chunk

    fake = _Graph()
    fake.graph = fake
    fake.propagator = fake
    return fake


def _wire(monkeypatch, tmp_path, fake, snapshots, final_render):
    """Install the fake graph and capture the real live view + final report."""
    real_update = display.update_display

    def spy_update(layout, *a, **k):
        real_update(layout, *a, **k)
        snapshots.append(_render_layout(layout))

    def capture_display(final_state):
        record = Console(record=True, width=200, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)
        monkeypatch.setattr(display, "console", record)
        monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "console", record)
        display_complete_report(final_state)
        final_render["text"] = record.export_text()

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "TradingAgentsGraph", lambda *a, **k: fake)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "update_display", spy_update)
    # A non-interactive Live: the layout is still built for real above.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli_run, "Live",
        type("L", (), {"__init__": lambda s, *a, **k: None,
                       "__enter__": lambda s: s, "__exit__": lambda s, *a: False})())
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "_offer_reports", lambda *a, **k: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr("cli.main.typer.prompt", lambda *a, **k: "N")
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run.sys, "stdin", type("S", (), {"isatty": lambda s: True})())
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "get_user_selections", lambda flags=None: {
        "ticker": "NVDA", "analysis_date": "2026-01-10",
        "analysts": [AnalystType.MARKET], "asset_type": "stock",
    })
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "_build_run_config", lambda s, c: {
        "data_cache_dir": str(tmp_path / "c"),
        "results_dir": str(tmp_path / "r"),
    })
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, "display_complete_report", capture_display)


def _risk_chunk(*, candidate_body, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids,
                evidence_index=None):
    """One stream chunk: debate histories plus the PM candidate and its internals."""
    return {
        "messages": [],
        "investment_debate_state": {
            "bull_history": "bull case", "bear_history": "bear case",
            "history": "", "current_response": "", "count": 2,
        },
        "investment_plan": "plan",
        "risk_debate_state": {
            "aggressive_history": "aggressive case",
            "conservative_history": "conservative case",
            "neutral_history": "neutral case",
            "history": "", "latest_speaker": "", "count": 3,
            "current_aggressive_response": "", "current_conservative_response": "",
            "current_neutral_response": "",
        },
        "final_trade_decision": candidate_body,
        "candidate_decision": candidate_body,
        "candidate_rating": candidate_rating,
        "candidate_argument_ids": candidate_argument_ids,
        "evidence_index": evidence_index,
    }


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_blocked_candidate_is_never_shown_and_only_blocked_renders(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """A refused candidate never appears in the live view; BLOCKED + reason does."""
    snapshots, final_render = [], {"text": ""}
    fake = _fake_graph([
        _risk_chunk(candidate_body=CANDIDATE_BODY, candidate_rating="Buy", candidate_argument_ids=[]),
    ])
    _wire(monkeypatch, tmp_path, fake, snapshots, final_render)

    cli_run.run_analysis()

    # The gate ran exactly once and refused (empty argument ids -> no evidence).
    assert fake.publish_calls == 1
    assert fake.publish_status == "BLOCKED"

    # The candidate body never appears in any live-view snapshot nor the final report.
    assert snapshots, "expected the live view to have been rendered"
    assert "buy now" not in "\n".join(snapshots)
    assert "buy now" not in final_render["text"]

    # The message area also never received the candidate body.
    message_text = "\n".join(str(c) for _ts, _t, c in display.message_buffer.messages)
    assert "buy now" not in message_text

    # The refusal is shown, with its reason, once the report is rendered.
    assert "BLOCKED" in final_render["text"]
    assert "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE" in final_render["text"]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_approved_candidate_is_shown_only_in_the_final_report(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

    cli_run.run_analysis()

    assert fake.publish_status == "APPROVED"

    # While streaming, the candidate body never appeared in the live view.
    assert snapshots
    assert "buy now" not in "\n".join(snapshots)
    # Only after approval does the official decision appear in the report.
    assert "buy now" in final_render["text"]

def test_blocked_candidate_is_never_shown_and_only_blocked_renders(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """A refused candidate never appears in the live view; BLOCKED + reason does."""
    snapshots = []
    fake = _fake_graph([
        _risk_chunk(candidate_body=CANDIDATE_BODY, candidate_rating="Buy", candidate_argument_ids=[]),

"""INV-01 checkpoint resume — a resumed run keeps its id and its chain verifies.

FR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a checkpointed run must be resumable **using the
project's own LangGraph checkpointer** (no ``msgpack`` dependency, no disabling the
checkpoint to dodge the problem). The evidence index is plain, serializable state,
so an interrupted run saves and a subsequent invocation on the same ticker+date
resumes it. The resumed run must:

- keep the **same run id** the interrupted run minted (ids are stable across a
  resume), so an argument accepted before the interruption is still resolvable;
- still resolve that argument's evidence, and so a legal decision is approved.

The interruption is real: the fake model raises inside the first Bull turn, after
the ``Index Evidence`` node has completed and saved. The second ``propagate`` call
resumes from that checkpoint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import pytest
from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult

from tradingagents.agents.schemas import DebateArgument, PortfolioDecision, PortfolioRating

REPORT = "The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend."

_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^- (ev:\S+)\s+\[", re.MULTILINE)
_ARGUMENT_LINE = re.compile(r"^- (arg:\S+)", re.MULTILINE)


class _CrashException(RuntimeError):
    """Raised from the first Bull turn of the first attempt to interrupt the run."""


class _CrashThenSucceedModel(BaseChatModel):
    """Crashes once mid-run; every later call succeeds.

    ``crashes`` is the number of times to raise before behaving normally. It is a
    plain class attribute so the two ``propagate`` calls share it.
    """

    crashes: int = 0

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "crash-then-succeed-fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        return self

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]
        if schema is DebateArgument:
            return _StructuredArgument()
        if schema is PortfolioDecision:
            return _StructuredDecision()
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,
                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,
                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])


class _StructuredArgument:
    def invoke(self, prompt):
        # The first Bull turn of the first attempt interrupts the run.
        if _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes > 0:
            _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes -= 1
            raise _CrashException("simulated interruption after the index was built")
        match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)
        return DebateArgument(
            argument="bull case",
            evidence_ids=[match.group(1)] if match else [],
        )


class _StructuredDecision:
    def invoke(self, prompt):
        match = _ARGUMENT_LINE.search(prompt)
        argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []
        return PortfolioDecision(
            rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,
            executive_summary="add",
            investment_thesis="breakout",
            argument_ids=argument_ids,
        )


class _FakeClient:
    def __init__(self, llm):
        self._llm = llm

    def get_llm(self):
        return self._llm


def _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path, crashes: int):
    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg
    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

    _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes = crashes
    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "create_tier_client",
                        lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_CrashThenSucceedModel()))
    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, "resolve_instrument_identity", lambda t: {
        "company_name": "NVIDIA Corporation", "sector": "Technology",
        "industry": "Semiconductors", "exchange": "NASDAQ", "quote_type": "EQUITY",
    })
    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    config.update({
        "data_cache_dir": str(tmp_path / "cache"),
        "results_dir": str(tmp_path / "results"),
        "memory_log_path": str(tmp_path / "memory.md"),
        # Checkpointing stays on: the whole point is to resume from it.
        "checkpoint_enabled": True,
    })
    return tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=("market",), debug=False, config=config)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_resume_after_interruption_keeps_run_id_and_approves(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path, crashes=1)

"""INV-01 cross-run isolation — two independent runs cannot cite each other.

FR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a run's id is minted fresh per run (not derived from
ticker+date), so two independent runs on the same instrument and date have
different ids. A decision in the second run that cites the first run's ``evidence_id``
or ``argument_id`` must be blocked — the reference does not resolve in the second
run's index.

Part 1 exercises the gate directly (deterministic). Part 2 checks the same at the
real ``propagate()`` level: two runs on the same ticker+date get different run ids.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate


def _index_with_accepted(run_id: str, report: str):
    """An index for ``run_id`` with one argument accepted against its evidence."""
    index = gate.build_evidence_index(run_id, {"market_report": report})
    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]
    argument_id = f"arg:bull:{run_id}:1"
    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(argument_id, "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev,)))
    return index, ev, argument_id


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_citing_another_runs_evidence_id_is_blocked():
    run_a, ev_a, arg_a = _index_with_accepted("run-A", "a")
    # Run B is a different run: its index has its own evidence and no accepted argument.
    run_b, _ev_b, _ = _index_with_accepted("run-B", "b")

    # Run B cannot claim run A's evidence, even by trying to build an identical arg.
    assert run_b.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(
        "arg:bull:run-B:1", "Bull Analyst", "x", (ev_a,),
    )) is False
    outcome = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), "Buy", (arg_a,))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_citing_another_runs_argument_id_is_blocked():
    _run_a, _ev_a, arg_a = _index_with_accepted("run-A", "a")
    run_b, ev_b, arg_b = _index_with_accepted("run-B", "b")

    # Run B resolves its own chain fine.
    owns = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), "Buy", (arg_b,))
    assert owns.status == gate.APPROVED

    # But run A's argument id is not in run B's index.
    outcome = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), "Buy", (arg_a,))
    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED
    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

def _wire(monkeypatch, tmp_path, fake, snapshots):
    """Install the fake graph and capture the real live view after each refresh.

    Each snapshot is recorded as ``(frame_text, gate_ran)`` where ``gate_ran`` is

After reading this entry point, follow [Prompt.md](Prompt.md) as the shared launch prompt. Plan first: name requirements and invariants, list exact files and contracts, specify independent normal/negative tests and rollback. Stop for recorded human approval of plan and tests before generating any implementation. Use the approved path list on each tool request. Configured writable paths are an outer limit; task approval may narrow them further. Governance, baseline history, existing tests and external data are frozen to the agent.

Verify imports and module boundaries, baseline regressions, each fit criterion and safety counterexamples. Offline runs use fixed fixtures and fake transport; live checks are separate and human-run. Record commands/results and actual interventions; mark unrun checks honestly. Submit a proposed change for human review; never merge, publish or widen permissions yourself.

Coordination: one owner per requirement and an explicitly agreed integrator for shared files. Follow the course OpenCode implementation workflow. Keep preparation/review distinct from implementation evidence and record the actual tools, scopes and sessions in the AI-use log. No auxiliary workflow may bypass course-role restrictions.
